verdicts.flaw_description: The reported 8-14 percent reductions come from a hand-picked slice of runs: "The figures cover the runs with the upgraded filter in service, and a quarter of each stack's runs were made with the filter bypassed" - so the 25 percent of post-upgrade runs with the filter out of circuit are dropped from the post figures while the earlier quarter's comparison presumably includes all runs. That is a narrower population than the claim, and it selects the runs most favourable to the upgrade.

Two of the four cases have outcome dates that precede the intervention: plot One was "boxed 3 June" but fledging is counted "by 27 March", and plot Three was "boxed 2 November" but counted "by 24 September". The boxes cannot have raised counts measured months before they were installed, and the seasons quoted (spring, autumn) do not match the installation dates either.

The germination figures are restricted to a favourable subset: "Rates cover the trays sown from seed that took a full coat, and about a fifth of each lot's trays were sown from partly coated seed" - so roughly 20 percent of each lot's trays are excluded from the post-coating scores while the previous spring sowing is scored whole. The 6-11 point gains therefore describe a narrower population than the lots the claim is about.

"Pass rates cover the students who attended every block, and about a quarter of each cohort missed at least one block" - so the 4-8 point gains are computed on only the full-attending three quarters of each cohort, compared against a previous term's whole-cohort pass rate. Perfect attenders are exactly the students most likely to pass anyway, so the comparison is between different populations.
